newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shekel weakens against dollar, basket.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shekel weakens against dollar, basket.

text.p: The Israeli shekel declined on Tuesday against the dollar and the basket of key foreign currencies in quiet trading, dealers said.
"The market was very quiet. The dollar rose in early trade because of one big deal in which shekels were converted into dollars," said a dealer at Bank Hapoalim.
"We have no further details about this deal and beside that nothing happened today," he said.

"Trading opened with high demand for the dollar and the dollar rose to 3.2350 shekels from which it fell to 3.2310. The dollar's rise might be the outcome of a single deal because afterwards the market remained very quiet and stable," said another dealer.

The representative rate for the dollar was fixed at 3.2310 shekels against 3.2270 on Monday. The basket, composed of the dollar, mark, pound sterling, French franc and yen, closed at 3.6439 shekels against 3.6357 on Monday.
On the crosses the shekel traded against the yen at 2.8989 shekels per 100 yen against 2.8930 on Monday and against the mark at 2.1497 shekels against 2.1414 on Monday.
In late afternoon the dollar was trading at 3.2315 shekels.
